candidates.title: Resolution preservation over architectural complexity: high-resolution patch-based semi-supervised learning for pancreas segmentation from CT images
candidates.abstract: Precise segmentation of the pancreas from computed tomography (CT) scans is critical for diagnosis and surgical planning but remains challenging due to the organ’s small volume (<0.5% of the abdomen), high anatomical variability, and low contrast with surround­ing tissues. Conventional deep learning methods typically downsample inputs to fit GPU memory, destroying fine-grained boundary information essential for small-organ delinea­tion. This study proposes a high-resolution patch-based framework that preserves native CT resolution (512 × 512) through 256 × 256 patch extraction with domain-specific Hounsfield unit (HU) windowing. A lightweight 2D U-Net (7.8M parameters) achieves 0.809±0.015 Dice (peak 0.849) on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) Task07 Pancreas dataset, com­petitive with nnU-Net (0.823 Dice, 88M parameters) and far above SAM (0.705) and Med­SAM (0.439). Five-fold cross-validation across all 281 volumes yields a population-level Dice of 0.630±0.025. Integrating uncertainty-aware mean teacher (UA-MT) semi-supervised learning recovers 99.3% of supervised performance using only 50% of labelled data, with reproducible results across three seeds (σ = 0.012). On 80 external TCIA volumes, UA-MT (0.603 Dice) out­performs the supervised model (0.544), demonstrating superior cross-domain generalisation.

candidates.title: Polyp-VSSD: A Pre-trained Transformer with Local-Global Joint VSSD Decoding for Polyp Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Early detection of colorectal polyps is essential for preventing colorectal cancer, making accurate polyp segmentation a key component in computer-aided diagnosis systems. However, existing endoscopic segmentation methods often exhibit limited representational capacity and insufficient integration of global and local contextual information. To address these limitations, we propose Polyp-VSSD, a novel local-global joint decoding framework built upon a pre-trained Transformer backbone for high-precision polyp segmentation. Polyp-VSSD leverages the strong feature expressiveness of large-scale visual pre-training and unifies global semantic modeling with local fine-grained reconstruction to enhance segmentation fidelity. Extensive experiments on multiple public endoscopic datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both Dice and IoU. On the EndoScene dataset, Polyp-VSSD achieves mIoU and mDice scores of 0.903 and 0.946, respectively, highlighting its robustness and strong generalization capability. This work presents an effective and scalable solution for intelligent endoscopic image analysis.

candidates.title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
candidates.abstract: Purpose: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status is a key biomarker relevant for prognostication and treatment decision making in metastatic breast cancer. Thus, the aim of this work was to explore whether HER2 status can be predicted directly from whole-brain post-contrast T1-weighted (T1w) MRI scans in breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM) using deep learning, and whether providing explicit tumour segmentation information improves prediction. Methods: Using the publicly available BCBM-Radiogenomics dataset, we analysed 135 patients, including 70 HER2+ and 65 HER2- patients. Three approaches were implemented and evaluated: a conventional radiomics model, a simple fully convolutional network (SFCN) using T1w MRI scans alone, and an SFCN using T1w MRI scans with an expert-derived tumour mask as an additional input channel. Results: The radiomics model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.602 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.528--0.677) while the SFCN achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.667 (95% CI, 0.63--0.71) using T1w MRI scans alone, which increased to 0.692 (95% CI, 0.58--0.81) when an explicit tumour mask was additionally provided. Conclusion: However, the modest performance across all approaches demonstrates the difficulty of predicting HER2 status from structural MRI scans alone. The difference between the segmentation-free and mask-guided SFCN models suggests that much of the predictive signal captured by the deep-learning model may be learned directly from whole-brain T1w MRI without requiring explicit tumour delineation. These findings support further investigation of segmentation-free deep-learning approaches as a potential non-invasive strategy to support HER2 status determination in BCBM.

candidates.title: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports
candidates.abstract: Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in clinical documentation, generating the rigorous, evidence-based reasoning required for unprecedented, atypical, and rare disease case reports remains a significant challenge. We present MedCaseAgent, an end-to-end agentic reasoning paradigm that bridges this gap by synthesizing publication-quality reports from unstructured clinical notes. MedCaseAgent leverages a hierarchical structure, integrating patient-level data mining with iterative, tool-integrated reasoning. By dynamically querying medical literature and knowledge bases, the agent maintains high clinical fidelity and assesses case novelty. The framework is inherently modular, supporting various backbone LLMs in a plug-and-play fashion. To facilitate this research, we release MedCase-150K, a large-scale multimodal clinical case-report corpus, and MedCase-Bench, a robust temporally held-out evaluation suite. We also introduce an open-source model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B and optimized specifically for this task. Under both LLM-judged and rule-based evaluation, MedCaseAgent outperforms existing general-purpose and specialized medical LLMs and agents. Blinded expert reviews and ablations further support the system's clinical relevance and evidence grounding.

candidates.title: Contrast-Gated Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of MedSAM for Skin-Tone-Robust Lesion Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Overview CG-MedSAM investigates contrast-conditioned parameter-efficient adaptation of MedSAM for skin-lesion segmentation across skin tones and imperfect bounding-box prompts. The project introduces residual bottleneck adapters modulated by a contrast signal computed within the prompt region. Research scope The manuscript evaluates segmentation quality, prompt perturbations, skin-tone subgroup performance, and contrast-conditioning ablations on ISIC 2018 and sDDI. Experimental findings and limitations should be interpreted using the manuscript and repository documentation. Supporting materials Project repository This deposit contains the author manuscript sourced from repository commit 1b73ab5b1bffa9a16dcbacacf8bc03a3ec42a433, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Datasets and model weights are not included. No journal acceptance or peer-review status is asserted by this deposit.

candidates.title: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation
candidates.abstract: The U-Net was presented in 2015. With its straight-forward and successful architecture it quickly evolved to a commonly used benchmark in medical image segmentation. The adaptation of the U-Net to novel problems, however, comprises several degrees of freedom regarding the exact architecture, preprocessing, training and inference. These choices are not independent of each other and substantially impact the overall performance. The present paper introduces the nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), which refers to a robust and self-adapting framework on the basis of 2D and 3D vanilla U-Nets. We argue the strong case for taking away superfluous bells and whistles of many proposed network designs and instead focus on the remaining aspects that make out the performance and generalizability of a method. We evaluate the nnU-Net in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge, which measures segmentation performance in ten disciplines comprising distinct entities, image modalities, image geometries and dataset sizes, with no manual adjustments between datasets allowed. At the time of manuscript submission, nnU-Net achieves the highest mean dice scores across all classes and seven phase 1 tasks (except class 1 in BrainTumour) in the online leaderboard of the challenge.

candidates.title: nnU-Net: Breaking the Spell on Successful Medical Image Segmentation.
candidates.abstract:
Fueled by the diversity of datasets, semantic segmentation is a popular
subfield in medical image analysis with a vast number of new methods being
proposed each year. This ever-growing jungle of methodologies, however, becomes
increasingly impenetrable. At the same time, many proposed methods fail to
generalize beyond the experiments they were demonstrated on, thus hampering the
process of developing a segmentation algorithm on a new dataset. Here we
present nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), a framework that automatically adapts itself to
any given new dataset. While this process was completely human-driven so far,
we make a first attempt to automate necessary adaptations such as
preprocessing, the exact patch size, batch size, and inference settings based
on the properties of a given dataset. Remarkably, nnU-Net strips away the
architectural bells and whistles that are typically proposed in the literature
and relies on just a simple U-Net architecture embedded in a robust training
scheme. Out of the box, nnU-Net achieves state of the art performance on six
well-established segmentation challenges. Source code is available at
https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnunet.

candidates.title: Efficient nnU-Net for Brain Tumor Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Brain tumors are one of the leading causes of death in adults. They come in various shapes and sizes from one patient to another. Sometimes they infiltrate surrounding normal tissues, making it challenging to delineate tumor boundaries. Despite extensive research, the prognosis is still low. Accurate and timely brain tumor segmentation is critical for treatment planning and disease progression monitoring. Automatic segmentation of brain tumors using deep learning methods has been shown to produce high-quality and reproducible segmentation results. Specifically, the encoder-decoder networks, like the U-Nets, have dominated the previous BraTS Challenges because of their superior performance. Due to the importance of high-quality segmentation, most state-of-the-art models focus more on pushing the boundaries of the current methods at the expense of computational complexity. The computational budget for practical applications is minimal, requiring technological solutions that balance accuracy and available computational resources. In this study, we extended the basic U-Net model in the nnU-Net by replacing the basic 3D convolution blocks with bottleneck units utilizing depthwise-separable convolutions. Furthermore, we introduced the shuffle attention mechanism in the skip connections to compensate for the slight loss in segmentation accuracy due to a reduction in number of parameters. Extensive experimental results of the BraTS 2020 dataset reviewed that the proposed modifications achieved competitive performance at a lower computational cost.

candidates.title: Brain tumor segmentation with advanced nnU-Net: Pediatrics and adults tumors
candidates.abstract: Automated brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance (MR) images plays a crucial role in precise diagnosis and treatment monitoring in brain tumor care. Leveraging the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge (BraTS) dataset, this paper introduces an extended version of the nnU-Net architecture for brain tumor segmentation, addressing both adult (Glioma) and pediatric tumors . Our methodology integrates innovative approaches to enhance segmentation accuracy . We incorporate residual blocks to capture complex spatial features , attention gates to emphasize informative regions and implement the Hausdorff distance (HD) loss for boundary-based segmentation refinement. The effectiveness of each enhancement is systematically evaluated through an ablation study using different configurations on the BraTS dataset. Results from our study highlight the significance of combining residual blocks, attention gates, and HD loss, achieving the best performance with a mean Dice and HD score of 83%, 3.8 and 71%, and 8.7 for Glioma and Pediatrics datasets, respectively. This advanced nnU-Net showcases the promising potential for accurate and robust brain tumor segmentation, offering valuable insights for enhanced clinical decision-making in pediatric brain tumor care.

candidates.title: Application of a Fusion Model Combining MRI-VASARI Features and ADC in Predicting the Molecular Subtypes of Adult-type Diffuse Gliomas
candidates.abstract: Objective: To develop a machine learning model integrating MRI visually accessible Rembrandt images (VASARI) features and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) parameters for the preoperative classification of the three subtypes of adult-type diffuse glioma. Methods: This study retrospectively enrolled 206 patients with pathologically confirmed adult-type diffuse glioma and divided them by scanner type into a training set (n=114) and an independent validation set (n=92). Tumor multi-region segmentation was conducted using nnU-Net, followed by extraction of VASARI features and ADC-related parameters. Recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV), XGBoost feature importance ranking, and incremental feature selection were applied to identify the optimal feature subset, and an XGBoost-based multiclass fusion model was subsequently constructed. Results: Twelve VASARI features and four ADC parameters (ADCmin, ADCmean, rADCmin, and rADCmean) differed significantly among the three subtypes. Eight features were finally selected for model construction. The fusion model achieved accuracies of 96.49% in the training set and 80.43% in the validation set. In the validation cohort, the area under the curves (AUCs) for predicting astrocytoma and glioblastoma were 0.96 and 0.97, respectively, both higher than those of the standalone VASARI and ADC models, while the AUC for oligodendroglioma was 0.59. SHAP analysis revealed that diffusion restriction, ADC parameters, and the margin of the non-enhancing region were the primary contributors to the model. Conclusion: The XGBoost-based fusion model integrating MRI-VASARI features and ADC demonstrated a high diagnostic performance in distinguishing glioblastoma and astrocytoma, but its ability to differentiate oligodendroglioma remained limited. Future studies should incorporate additional imaging features, such as calcification, to further improve the model performance.

candidates.title: A multi-task learning-based network for detecting three-dimensional osteometric landmarks of the shoulder joint
candidates.abstract: Background Mirror-based preoperative planning for total shoulder arthroplasty relies on accurate three-dimensional (3D) localization of bony landmarks on the contralateral, anatomically intact shoulder. Manual annotation is time-consuming and shows inter- and intra-observer variability. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a multi-task deep-learning network for automated 3D bony landmark detection on contralateral shoulder CT. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 179 patients with intact contralateral shoulder CT scans were split at the patient level into training (n = 125), validation (n = 18), and test (n = 36) sets. We developed a dual-decoder 3D BiFormer-UNet for humerus and scapula segmentation and heatmap-based localization of 14 anatomical landmarks. A cross-task feature-fusion (CtFF) module transferred bone-structural guidance from the segmentation decoder to the landmark decoder. The network was trained end-to-end using a composite loss comprising hard-negative-mining heatmap regression, a geometric structure constraint, distance-aware similarity learning, and auxiliary segmentation loss. Landmark localization was evaluated using MRE and SDR at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, while segmentation was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Per-case MRE was compared with four 3D baseline models using paired tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. Results In the 36-case test set, the proposed model achieved an MRE of 2.1 ± 1.2 mm (95% CI, 1.7–2.5 mm) and SDRs of 72.0%, 81.8%, 90.3%, and 96.7% at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, respectively. Its MRE was significantly lower than those of 3D U-Net, V-Net, 3D HRNet adaptation, and H3DE-Net (all Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05). On the test set, the auxiliary segmentation branch achieved mean Dice coefficients of 0.83 ± 0.05 for the humerus and 0.78 ± 0.07 for the scapula. Internally defined center landmarks, particularly the humeral head rotation center, anatomical neck center, and proximal and distal medullary canal centers, showed larger localization errors (2.3–2.6 mm) than most surface landmarks. Conclusion The proposed multi-task framework demonstrated promising 3D landmark localization performance on intact contralateral shoulder CT by integrating global anatomical context with bone-structural guidance. It may serve as an upstream localization component for mirror-based shoulder arthroplasty planning, although external validation is required before clinical use.

candidates.title: Interpretable and backpropagation-free Green Learning for efficient multi-task echocardiographic segmentation and classification
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable, backpropagation-free multi-task Green Learning (MTGL) framework for automated echocardiographic analysis. It addresses the need for reliable left ventricular (LV) segmentation and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) classification while reducing the parameter burden, energy demand and opacity associated with conventional deep learning (DL) models. The objective is to determine whether a unified feed-forward framework can deliver clinically relevant accuracy, computational efficiency and interpretable feature representations. Design/methodology/approach The framework uses a four-hop, PCA/Saab-based unsupervised VoxelHop encoder followed by a coarse-to-fine XGBoost residual-regression decoder for LV segmentation and a pooled multi-scale XGBoost classifier for three-class LVEF classification. Experiments used the predefined EchoNet-Dynamic training, validation and test partitions. MTGL was evaluated against matched 3D V-Net, 3D U-Net, 3D UNETR and 3D nnU-Net baselines using classification accuracy and balanced accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Findings On the EchoNet-Dynamic test set, MTGL achieved 94.3% accuracy for three-class LVEF classification, and 0.912 DSC for LV segmentation, outperforming all compared baselines. It used 1.13 million parameters, versus 10.47–49.08 million for the DL comparators, and showed the lowest measured training energy use and carbon emissions. Hop ablation further showed complementary multi-scale information, with the full feature set yielding the highest classification accuracy. Originality/value Unlike end-to-end backpropagation-based DL methods, MTGL combines an unsupervised linear VoxelHop representation with task-specific XGBoost decoders in a single multi-task echocardiographic pipeline. The PCA/Saab direct current and alternating current feature decomposition enables direct inspection of learned spatial and spatiotemporal signals, linking shallow features to anatomical boundaries and deeper features to global contractile dynamics. The study therefore demonstrates that a compact, interpretable Green Learning system can jointly support LV segmentation and LVEF grouping with strong in-domain performance and lower measured training environmental cost.
